The '''Strontium Raid''' was a confrontation that took place in [[15,480 BBY]] at the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="CSWE Abhean">{{CSWECite|I|6|Abhean}}</ref> [[Abhean/Legends|Abhean]]. The planet was situated along the portion of the [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] known as the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] that was under the control of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="EGTW" />

The Strontium Raid was a late engagement of the [[Second Alsakan Conflict]], a war that had commenced approximately [[16,100 BBY|six centuries]] earlier, lasted for another [[15,400 BBY|eighty years]], and was one of a fourteen-[[Millennium/Legends|millennia]]-long [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|series]] of wars over [[Politics/Legends|political]] control of the Republic between Coruscant, the planet [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], and their respective allies.<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:StrontiumRealWorld.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A sample of pure real-world strontium]]
The Strontium Raid was introduced in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', authored by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]].<ref name="EGTW" /> In the real world, [[Wikipedia:Strontium|strontium]] is a [[Wikipedia:Chemical element|chemical element]] and [[Wikipedia:Metal|metal]]. Its [[Wikipedia:Chemical compound|compounds]] are used in the manufacture of [[Wikipedia:Ferrite (magnet)|ferrite magnets]] as well as in [[Wikipedia:Fireworks|fireworks]], [[Wikipedia:Flare|flares]], and [[Wikipedia:Tracer ammunition|tracer ammunition]], and the [[Wikipedia:Radioactive decay|radioactive]] [[Wikipedia:Isotope|isotope]] [[Wikipedia:Stronntium-90|strontium-90]] has been used as a power source in [[Wikipedia:Radioisotope thermoelectric generator|radioisotope thermoelectric generators]].<ref name="StrontiumBritannica">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/strontium|text=Strontium &#124; Chemical Element, Health, & Industrial Applications|author=The Editors of Encyclopædia Britannica|date=2024-03-01|work=[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|''Encyclopædia Britannica'']]|archivedate=20240702181116}}</ref>
